newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S SPOORNET FOLLOWS MINES TO BRAZIL.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S SPOORNET FOLLOWS MINES TO BRAZIL.

text.p: South Africa's state-owned rail network Spoornet was following local mining houses to Brazil to market its expertise in hauling minerals and metals, Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau said on Monday.
"Over the years Spoornet has developed world market leadership in the running of heavy haul trains that carry minerals such as coal and iron ore," she said in the debate on her 1997/98 budget.

"The technologies and the competencies that Spoornet has developed over the years are not only sought after the world over but provide the company with a competitive tool that has the potential of carving out a niche market for Spoornet in the global market."
It was therefore bidding to operate freight and heavy haul rail systems in Brazil, where many South African mining companies had started operating since the removal of sanctions.
"The advantage of this approach is that Spoornet has serviced these companies at home and thus has a rapport with them that will minimise problems," Sigcau said.
"From their side they have a transportation partners that is as committed as they are to the success of the project."
